surfaces.part: control deck with buttons and joystick
lower cabinet front with coin door

answer.evidence: This is a pair of upright arcade cabinets seen from the front, not a container with an opening, so the kind does not match. The marquee and screen are vertical faces. The only horizontal surface on the cabinet body is the control deck at rows 21-24. It is wider (32 vs 28) and carries buttons, with a lighter front-edge line at row 24 and a dark shadow at rows 25-26. Below it is a lower front face of about 10 rows (26-35) with a coin door. The top of the cabinet at rows 0-3 shows no horizontal surface. The stools at rows 37-43 have ellipse seat tops (widths 12, 16, 20, 20, 20, 20, 16).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a pair of small arcade cabinets with red stools. Its tile density is respectable: 14 visible tones per tile against 9-20 for the references, and only 6% near-flat coverage, so it is not a flat fill. The weakness is the outline. 82% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, and the cabinets are wrapped in a dark, almost colourless line. That is the 'sticker' look, unlike the references, where the hedge (0%), cheese stall (1%) and roofed well (33%) use tinted, material-toned edges. The cabinet bodies also read as 2-3 lightness steps (dark body, mid panel, small highlights), well below the 5-6 steps on the stall and well. The stools are simple, with little grain. The tone count passes, but the near-black outline and shallow ramps do not match the Beodeul standard.
